newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Crimea peninsula names new premier.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Crimea peninsula names new premier.

text.p: Parliament in Ukraine's autonomous Crimean peninsula on Wednesday named Anatoly Franchuk, a relative of President Leonid Kuchma by marriage, as prime minister.
Deputies voted by 77 to two to appoint Franchuk, who held the post in 1994 and 1995 and whose son is married to Kuchma's daughter.
Franchuk, 62, replaces Arkady Demidenko, who had been blamed for economic problems and faced repeated no-confidence votes.
The mostly Russian-populated peninsula is claimed by Russian nationalists and has been the focus of tensions between Moscow and Kiev since the Soviet Union broke up in 1991.
Deputies needed Kiev's approval to change the prime minister and last week the cabinet gave its consent.
